headline: Diriyah, Royal Commission and Hilton join Riyadh hospitality summit
deck: Diriyah, the Royal Commission for Riyadh City and Six Flags Qiddiya share a speaker list with Hilton, Accor, Radisson and Ritz-Carlton — the two halves of a hotel deal.
excerpt: The Hospitality Leaders Summit at Riyadh's hotel exhibition brings Saudi giga-project developers together with the international operators who will run their hotels.
content:
The Hospitality Leaders Summit, running inside the Hotel and Hospitality Expo at Riyadh's convention centre from 15 September, has assembled a speaker list that maps both sides of a hotel transaction — the parties who build and the parties who operate.

On the development side the organiser has confirmed Abdullah Hassan Al Fryan, executive director and tourism senior director at the Royal Commission for Riyadh City; Christian Krollig, senior director of feasibilities at Diriyah Company; and Hisham AlAali, vice president of human resources and shared services at Six Flags Qiddiya City. On the operating side are Elie Badawi, regional director for Saudi Arabia at Hilton; Ahmad Yousry Elbeheiry, senior director of development at Accor; Hans Konings, general manager at Radisson Hotel Group; Mazen Allam, area general manager at The Ritz-Carlton Hotel Company; Tariq Yousef Dowidar, regional vice president for Saudi Arabia at Aleph Hospitality; Mina Anziani, chief operating officer at Kerten Hospitality; and Nuran Kilani, vice president of commercial operations at Time Hotels.

The pairing is the point. A Saudi giga-project does not operate its own hotels; it builds them and contracts an operator to run them under a brand. The terms of that contract — management fee, brand standards, capital commitments, performance thresholds — determine a great deal about what the building has to contain and what it costs to deliver. Putting a Diriyah feasibility director on a platform with Hilton's and Accor's development leads is putting the two sides of that negotiation in view of the suppliers who will eventually be specified into the result.

The presence of a feasibilities director specifically is worth noting. Feasibility is the stage at which a hotel's positioning, room count and star grade are fixed, and it is upstream of everything a supplier cares about. Al Othaim Investment's chief hospitality officer, Ashraf Qasem, appears on the same list, representing the domestic investor side rather than the giga-project or the international operator.

The summit's declared themes run across investment and destination development, Saudi cultural identity in hospitality, technology and operations, supply chain and procurement, alternative hospitality investments, food and beverage as a growth driver, and culinary talent development. Culinary is unusually well represented among the speakers: Bilal Saleh, regional chef for Hilton in Saudi Arabia; Omar Alazeeh, executive chef at Hyatt Place AlUla; Felipe Alvear, culinary director at Grand Hyatt The Red Sea; and Daniele Chiari of Royal Protocol Hospitality and Catering, alongside training figures including Dr Jorge Arnanz of King Faisal International Academy and Amna Alyamani of Alkhaleej Training and Education.

One gap is worth flagging. The organiser has published speaker names and thematic pillars but not a timed agenda: the session schedule pages were live but unpopulated five days before opening. Speaker lists and themes exist; the running order does not.

Speaker names and titles here come from the organiser's own summit page.
